name: @olai/plugin-api
//name: IT WAS `@olai/plugins`, in `packages/plugins/`, and the rename is what made room for the tenants. It then held two things at once — the INTERFACE a plugin is written against, and the REGISTRY that names every plugin — and the second half left for `@olai/bundle` when the first became something a plugin IMPORTS. What is here now is the interface and nothing else: the services a plugin names, the events it listens on, and the shapes it hands over. It imports no plugin, which is the whole of why a plugin may import it.
//exports: TWO DOORS, and the split is about which PROCESS opens them rather than about which package does. The ROOT is what a BROWSER half is written against — the dressings, the chrome slots and the marks, whose fields return `JSX.Element` — plus the shapes both halves share. `./services` is what a SERVER half is written against: the Cordis service classes a plugin names in its `inject`, the events it listens on, and the declaration merging that types `ctx.vault` and `ctx.surfaces`. Neither door reaches a plugin, so the graph claims the fence used to make about this package are now claims about `@olai/bundle`; what is left here for the fence to hold is that the SERVICES door pulls no `solid-js`, which is the same hazard one door over — a server that reached a browser face through the interface would evaluate a `.tsx` and die on `react/jsx-dev-runtime` before it served anything.
//: WHAT A PLUGIN IS WRITTEN AGAINST — src/plugin.ts argues the browser half, src/contract.ts the shapes both halves share, and src/services.ts the runtime a server half installs itself into. The registry that names the plugins is `@olai/bundle`.
//dependencies: `effect` is for the schemas a contributed member is declared in; `solid-js` is TYPES ONLY — `JSX.Element` is the return of every face a dressing or a chrome slot names, and a type import puts no runtime on any graph. NO plugin, which is the direction that lets a plugin import this package at all. NO `@olai/surface`, deliberately and structurally: surface depends on THIS package, so a dependency back would be the cycle the whole arrangement is shaped to make unrepresentable. NO `@olai/format` for the same reason one floor over — the kind table travels as DATA, handed down by the server, and a floor package that imported the vocabulary would be the format learning what a terminal is. `cordis` is not declared and is not an omission: it is hydrated from the npins pin (nix/cordis.nix) into the root node_modules, the way every `@kolu/*` member is.
